_meta.indication: Preventive treatment of migraine in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 6-month trial; patients randomized 2:1:1 to placebo, galcanezumab 120 mg monthly (240 mg loading dose), or 240 mg monthly.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 to 65 years with a diagnosis of migraine for at least 1 year experiencing 4 to 14 migraine headache days per month (episodic migraine).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change from baseline in the number of monthly migraine headache days over the 6-month treatment period.
pivotal_trials.n: 858 patients randomized; in the primary efficacy table EMGALITY 120 mg N=210 and placebo N=425 (galcanezumab 240 mg N=208).
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in monthly migraine headache days -4.7 (120 mg) vs -2.8 placebo; difference from placebo -1.9 days, p<0.001.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 6-month trial of identical design to EVOLVE-1; patients randomized 2:1:1 to placebo, galcanezumab 120 mg monthly (240 mg loading dose), or 240 mg monthly.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with a history of episodic migraine (4 to 14 migraine days per month).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change from baseline in the number of monthly migraine headache days over the 6-month treatment period.
pivotal_trials.n: 915 patients randomized; in the primary efficacy analysis placebo N=450, galcanezumab 120 mg N=226, 240 mg N=220.
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in monthly migraine headache days -4.3 (120 mg) vs -2.3 placebo; difference from placebo -2.0 days, p<0.001.

pivotal_trials.design: 3-month randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 2:1:1 to placebo, galcanezumab 120 mg monthly (240 mg loading dose), or 240 mg monthly.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 to 65 with chronic migraine (at least 15 headache days per month with at least 8 migraine days per month).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change from baseline in the number of monthly migraine headache days over the 3-month treatment period.
pivotal_trials.n: 1113 patients randomized; in the primary analysis galcanezumab 120 mg N=273, placebo N=538 (galcanezumab 240 mg N=274).
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in monthly migraine headache days -4.8 (120 mg) vs -2.7 placebo; difference from placebo -2.1 days, p<0.001.

key_safety: No serious safety issues with clear causal relationship identified; most common adverse reaction was injection site reactions (18% galcanezumab 120 mg vs 13% placebo). Hypersensitivity reactions (rash, urticaria, dyspnea) reported.
target_moa: Humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody that binds the calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) ligand and blocks its binding to the CGRP receptor.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the applicant had provided substantial evidence of effectiveness from three adequate and well-controlled studies and the safety profile was acceptable.

description.text: Added treatment of episodic cluster headache in adults

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for the use of Emgality for the treatment of episodic cluster headache in adults.

summary.text: BLA submitted 9/27/17 and filed with a Standard review designation; approved as a traditional full approval, not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: BLA 761603 was submitted on 9/27/17. The applicant considered that the application included all the safety data needed to support a full review. (See discussion in Section 8.2 Adequacy of the database). The BLA was filed with a Standard review designation on 11/24/17.

This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it was clear that the applicant had provided substantial evidence of effectiveness from three adequate and well-controlled studies, using clinical trial designs similar to those for previously approved migraine drugs.

requirement.text: 3498-1: Deferred pediatric randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study under PREA assessing pharmacokinetics, efficacy and safety for preventive treatment of episodic migraine in children and adolescents ages 6 through 17 years.

citations.quote: 3498-1 Deferred pediatric randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study under PREA to assess the pharmacokinetics (Part A), and efficacy and safety (Part B) for the preventive treatment of episodic migraine in children and adolescents ages 6 through 17 years.

requirement.text: 3498-2: Deferred pediatric randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled efficacy and safety study under PREA for preventive treatment of chronic migraine in adolescents ages 12 through 17 years.

citations.quote: 3498-2 Deferred pediatric randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled efficacy and safety study under PREA for the preventive treatment of chronic migraine in adolescents ages 12 through 17 years.

requirement.text: 3498-3: Prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with migraine exposed to Emgality during pregnancy with two unexposed control populations.

citations.quote: 3498-3 Conduct prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses in the United States that compare the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with migraine exposed to Emgality during pregnancy with two unexposed control populations: one consisting of women with migraine who have not been exposed to Emgality before or during pregnancy and the other consisting of women without migraine.

requirement.text: 3498-4: Pregnancy outcomes study using a different design (e.g., retrospective cohort or case control) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, preterm births, and small-for-gestational-age births in women exposed to Emgality during pregnancy vs an unexposed control population.

citations.quote: 3498-4 Conduct a pregnancy outcomes study using a different study design than provided for in PMR 3498-3 (for example, a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data or a case control study) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, preterm births, and small-for-gestational-age births in women exposed to Emgality during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.
